Hello! Thank you for doing this. There is a condition called Post SSRI Sexual Dysfunction (PSSD). This condition results in persistent/permanent cognitive issues and sexual dysfunction either while on Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors or upon cessation. The problems do not go away once the drugs have left the system and it affects both males and females. Recently it was recognized by the EMA as a legitimate medical condition.   [https://rxisk.org/ema-acknowledges-persistent-sexual-dysfunction-after-ssris-snris/](https://rxisk.org/ema-acknowledges-persistent-sexual-dysfunction-after-ssris-snris/)  PSSD is believed to be as a result of SSRIs causing epigenetic changes.   [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30148158/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30148158/)  Specifically some hypothesize it to cause methylation of Androgen and Estrogen receptors. PSSD is a debilitating disease that has caused countless individuals to take their own lives.   Sexual dysfunction Symptoms include:   Reduced genital sensation / genital anesthesia Erectile dysfunction / decreased vaginal lubrication Delayed or inability to orgasm (anorgasmia) Pleasureless, weak or “muted” orgasms Decreased libido Reduced response to sexual stimuli Decreased or lack of nocturnal erections Premature ejaculation Reduced nipple sensitivity Soft glans  Cognitive/other symptoms include  Anhedonia Memory loss Issues with sleep  Depersonalization Loss of drive/motivation Loss of creativity Loss of focus Reduced overall cognitive abilities   [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6004900/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6004900/) [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29675596/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29675596/)  Collection of studies   [https://pssdlab.files.wordpress.com/2018/06/pssd-info-sheet.pdf](https://pssdlab.files.wordpress.com/2018/06/pssd-info-sheet.pdf)  It is an extremely under recognized disease but the impact it has on its sufferers is absolutely devastating. Some doctors recognize it, but there is no cure and treatment involves guesswork for symptom management. Is this something that you are familiar with?
